# @flatten-js/spatial-graph 2.0

A 2D simple undirected graph using private Graphology storage and RBush
candidate indexes. Node positions are Cartesian Point2D tuples. Public graph
queries return immutable SpatialNode/SpatialEdge snapshots, with no graph pointer.

Install @flatten-js/spatial-graph and peer @flatten-js/core. ESM/CJS declarations
ship for Node.js 22+. Raw TypeScript examples require Node 22.18+.

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';
const graph = new SpatialGraph();
graph.addEdge([[0, 0], [10, 0]], {label: 'link'});
graph.addEdge([[10, 0], [10, 10]]);
const node = graph.getNode([10, 0]);
node?.type; // corner
const edge = graph.getEdgeBetween([0, 0], [10, 0]);
edge?.midpoint; // [5, 0]
edge?.length; // 10
if (node) {
  graph.moveNode(node, [12, 0]);
  node.point; // retained [10, 0]
  graph.getNode([10, 0]); // null
}
```

## Contracts

- Point2D = readonly [x,y]; Segment2D = readonly [Point2D,Point2D]. NodeInput and
  EdgeInput also accept same-graph snapshots resolved against current membership.
- Exact finite coordinates are default. coordinatePrecision 0 opts into the old
  integer grid; 0..15 quantizes decimals with Math.round and normalizes -0.
  Scaled values must remain safe integers. Use getNodeKey, never build keys manually.
- Coordinates define node equality within one graph. Moving removes/recreates or
  merges destinations. Snapshot equality ignores metadata and object identity.
- Snapshot coordinates/top-level attributes are copied and frozen. Nested data
  remains shared unless cloneNodeAttributes/cloneEdgeAttributes hooks are supplied.
- Classification: isolated=0, stub=1, intermediate=straight degree 2,
  corner=bent degree 2, junction=3+. straightAngleToleranceDeg defaults to 1e-7;
  positionTolerance defaults to 1e-9. Tolerances never affect equality.
- Metadata cannot override geometry. User weight remains data; default routing
  uses derived length. Required generic node fields require createNodeAttributes;
  required attribute arguments cannot be omitted. Label setters preserve declared
  string unions; null removal requires an undefined-compatible label. Graph
  metadata has its own API.
- Missing scalar/element queries return null, collections [], membership/removal
  false. Bad input throws before mutation. Move of a missing node throws.
- addEdge/addEdges report added/existing/collapsed; duplicate metadata is retained.
  addNode upserts. mergeNodeAttributes updates existing nodes only.
- moveNodes is simultaneous and atomic for invalid inputs. Destination metadata
  wins, then smallest canonical source key. Edge conflicts use original endpoint
  pairs. Conflict callbacks execute during planning and cannot mutate the graph.
- splitEdge validates exact and canonical containment; missing/endpoint splits
  are no-ops. IDs are copied, never rewritten. splitAttributes customizes them.
- joinNode preserves straight degree-2 geometry and rejects existing neighbor
  edges; collapseDegree2Node explicitly permits changing bends/triangles.
- findPaths covers every edge once and includes cycles. Components include isolated
  nodes. findTerminalPaths measures degree within the induced subset.

## Recipes

```ts
const path = graph.getShortestPath([0, 0], [12, 0], {algorithm: 'astar'});
const length = path?.length;
const nearest = graph.findNearestEdge([4, 3]);
if (nearest) {
  graph.splitEdge(nearest.edge, nearest.point);
  graph.addEdge([[4, 3], nearest.point]);
}
const report = graph.planarize();
for (const node of graph.getNodesByType('intermediate')) graph.joinNode(node);
const restored = SpatialGraph.fromJSON(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(graph.export())));
const detached = graph.toGraphology();
const imported = SpatialGraph.fromGraphology(detached);
```

Nearest results include exact point, distance, t (source-to-target), and clamped.
RBush lower-bound search evaluates exact geometry; ties follow insertion order.
Use {scan:true} for the reference. Empty graphs return null. All geometry edits
update indexes; metadata edits do not.

Routing defaults to Dijkstra/length. Cost callbacks return finite nonnegative
numbers or null to close an edge. A* supports reopening; custom heuristics must
be admissible, finite, nonnegative, zero at destination. Default A* heuristic is
Euclidean for length, zero for custom costs. Length and cost are independent.
route(fromPoint,toPoint,{maxSnapDistance}) returns virtual traversal points and
snap results, uses geometric cost, and does not modify graph/revision.

Planarize handles crossings/T-junctions/overlaps. Unrepresentable grid crossings
return unresolved points without editing. mergeNearbyNodes forms transitive
clusters with canonical representatives; maxDisplacement can exceed tolerance.

Spatial JSON schema='spatial-graph', version=2 includes options, explicit nodes,
edges, metadata. Metadata must be JSON-compatible for JSON.stringify round trips.
import replaces by default; {merge:true} uses matching policies and union rules.
fromLegacyJSON(data,{coordinatePrecision:0}) returns {graph,report} with collisions
and collapsed edge counts; legacy weight stays metadata.

Graphology adapters are detached O(V+E) copies with top-level x/y and length and
nested data. fromGraphology validates topology/geometry and accepts metadata
mapping callbacks. Internal routing uses private Graphology directly.
Flatten methods explicitly contain Flatten in their names. Segments and straight
Multilines are supported; unsupported arcs/rays/lines throw before insertion.
fromGeoJSON accepts Point/LineString/MultiLineString features, maps properties to
metadata, and rejects extra dimensions unless dropExtraDimensions is set.
Supply onReport to inspect insertion outcomes, including precision collapses.
toGeoJSON emits per-edge LineStrings plus isolated Points, without geodesic claims.

Full API, runnable asserting recipes, and migration guidance: README.md,
examples/, docs/library-refactoring-audit.md. 1.x NxPoint/NxEdge and raw inherited
Graphology methods were removed; use tuples for geometry and snapshots for members.
